geometry_edits.rationale: Replace the arbitrary sawtooth striping with a clearer gym-like long-span roof family that better expresses section and daylight.
Preserve the long horizontal hall emphasis and keep the section aligned to the building's dominant axis.
Keep the access-edge carve on the verified frontage side so the ground response remains tied to public entry.
Open the frontage carve more decisively to strengthen public void and reduce the sealed-box reading.

rationale: The candidate is more coherent than a random fragment set, but it still reads as a horizontally layered object rather than one clearly legible gymnasium hall. Across the four views the mass is consistent enough to avoid a view-only success, yet the roof/section logic is mostly repetitive striping and low steps rather than an explicit long-span or daylight-bearing gym section. The blue frontage is acknowledged only weakly: the mass does not open with a strong public void, entry seam, or court aligned to the access edge, so the ground response feels sealed and semantically neutral. The dominant form is also somewhat over-composed, with several surface bands competing instead of one primary hall plus subordinate threshold. Reference resonance is moderate with low pavilion halls and terraced sports precedents, but the candidate does not yet achieve the open threshold or section clarity those references demonstrate. Because this program is a gymnasium, the visible mass should more clearly support a clear-span interior and a legible entry/service hierarchy; that relationship is not yet convincing enough for program_fit_hard_pass.

warnings: Parcel containment appears acceptable in the shown frames; no visible hard breach detected.
The access edge response is misaligned in spirit: the frontage remains mostly sealed rather than forming a readable entry void/court.
Sectional read is weak for a gymnasium; the stepped roof does not yet communicate long-span structure or daylight logic.
Do not treat the coherent top view alone as sufficient; the form needs to hold up in elevation and section as well.
